## Laser Induced Peptide Fibrillation Experiment

I used fs-laser at its maximum power to induce peptide fibrillation. I tried 
to scan a small ROI or even a single point for maximum of 4 minutes. We tried to 
at the substrate and buffer interface, in the bulk buffer and at the buffer-air interface. 
We didn't observe new TAT nucleation or fibrillation in all three cases. 
Furthermore, we have also tried two different TAT concentration (low and high). I am doing some 
literature search to see if I can find some criteria for the experimental 
parameters, such laser power, exposure time, TAT concentration and focusing position to 
induce initiate nucleation, droplets or fibrillation.

## iSCAT Noise Source

I have recorded the vibration with the iSCAT system (PhotonFocus camera) to compare 
with the recording with my phone of beam visible vibrations. There is a clear 
20 Hz frequency in the image. I did try to find the source but so far I was not 
able to find where the 20 Hz frequency is coming from. I have some new ideas that 
I will try next week to find the source of the vibration.

## LSCM-iSCAT Image Calibration

I cleaned a substrate and scratch it with a diamond tip. I dropped dilute solution of Cy5 
where the dye molecules will stick to the scratches. Furthermore, I then imaged the sample with confocal and iSCAT.
I then used the scratches as fiducial markers to calibrate the confocal image with the iSCAT image. 
I can see the emission from the Cy5 molecules in the LSCM image and the scattering from the scratches in the iSCAT image.
The images are higher correlated and with slight adjustment on steering mirror to the iSCAT camera, 
I can find the position that matched the one in LSCM image. 

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.08.24 (Amir Fathi - Single Emitter, iSAT Noise, GNPs on BMP SLB)\lscm-iscat-calib.png)

::: {.column width="65%"}

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.08.24 (Amir Fathi - Single Emitter, iSAT Noise, GNPs on BMP SLB)\multistep-analysis.png)

::: {.column width="35%"}

I have analyzed another two samples to check for the multistep photobleaching. 
There are some tracks that show multistep photobleaching but typically compare to the 
number of tracks there are only less than 4% of the tracks that show multistep photobleaching.
This indicates that the majority of the tracks are from single emitters. Left: 25% BMP with TAT-R - 2026-07-08
Right: 50% BMP with TAT 2026-06-10.
